column1: # name<TAB>setup<TAB>arguments[<TAB>refusal] (line RG items D5b-1 and D5b-2). Each row runs in a copy of in/: the setup steps
# (" ; "-separated: makembindex ARGS and makeblastdb ARGS with LOSAT's programs, put FILE OFFSET VALUE, cut FILE SIZE,
# cp FROM TO, rm FILE, cat OUT FROM... (the bytes of the FROM files), join OUT TITLE FROM... (one FASTA record ">TITLE" with
# the sequence lines of the FROM files); @TESTS@ in a step is LOSAT/tests), then blastn with the arguments (their first
# NAME=value words are variables of the run).
# ncbi/<name>.{out,err,rc}: NCBI BLAST+ 2.17.0 (the official Linux x64 release, local oracle), 2026-11-21, with NCBI's makembindex
# and makeblastdb for the setup: the rows above "D5b-2 rows" by ad-RG-D5-4 with remaining-gaps-20261112/D/d5/fixture/freeze_d5b1.py,
# the rest by ad-RG-D5-5's subagent with freeze_d5b2.py there (which re-freezes every row; in/'s D5b-2 files: its --make-in-d5b2,
# gen2.py and gen_d5b2.py). Rows on databases made in the setup print no database date (outfmt 6).
# A row with a refusal is one where NCBI searches with an index in a way LOSAT does not (a mixed search, a two-hit search,
# -db_hard_mask) or reads one in an undefined way (or crashes): LOSAT refuses with
# "-use_index true with <refusal> is not supported by LOSAT's BLASTN"; NCBI's output stays for the lines that take them.
